title: Trump Media Sells 100K Monthly Subscription for Early Truth Social Access
description_short: Trump Media Sells 100K Monthly Subscription for Early Truth Social Access
description_medium: Trump Media said it had signed more than ten agreements, mostly with high-frequency trading firms, to provide Truth Social posts through a data feed seconds before public display. CNN reported prices of $60,000–$100,000 a month. Senators Elizabeth Warren and Adam Schiff asked regulators to investigate the arrangement’s legality; the report records no legal finding of insider trading.
description_long: Trump Media and Technology Group told investors on an August 2026 earnings call that it had signed more than ten customer agreements, mostly with high-frequency trading firms, for early access to Truth Social posts. The company said customers would pay between $60,000 and $100,000 a month for an application programming interface that delivers posts fractions of a second before the public feed. Traders use algorithms to react to market-sensitive posts about tariffs, national security and executive orders, so a brief head start could affect when they buy or sell. The company said it had recognized only modest revenue so far and was speaking with news organizations and AI companies about access. Senators Elizabeth Warren and Adam Schiff had urged regulators to examine whether the arrangement complied with securities law, calling it an abuse of presidential office. CNN reported no regulatory finding or court decision that the service constituted insider trading. The documented event is a paid data product offering early access to the president’s posts, alongside questions about market fairness and the use of presidential communications; the alleged legal violation remained unresolved.
subcategory: Paid early access to presidential social-media posts

preserved_fields.description_short: Trump Media Sells 100K Monthly Subscription for Early Truth Social Access

title: Kari Lake Voice of America Shutdown Voided as Illegal Under Federal Vacancies Act
description_short: Kari Lake Voice of America Shutdown Voided as Illegal Under Federal Vacancies Act
description_medium: The supplied synopsis describes two rulings by Judge Royce Lamberth: a March 8 decision finding Kari Lake’s acting leadership of the U.S. Agency for Global Media unlawful and voiding 2025 actions, followed by a March 17 order returning 1,042 Voice of America employees to work. The only linked Reuters story is dated March 8 and could not be retrieved, so it cannot verify the later order or its scope.
description_long: The supplied account describes two related court actions concerning Kari Lake’s leadership of the U.S. Agency for Global Media and cuts at Voice of America. On March 8, U.S. District Judge Royce Lamberth reportedly ruled that Lake’s tenure as acting chief executive violated the Federal Vacancies Reform Act and the Appointments Clause because she was not employed by the agency when its prior chief resigned. The account says the ruling voided actions Lake took in 2025, including mass layoffs of VOA journalists. It then describes a separate March 17 order directing 1,042 sidelined employees to return to work by the following Monday. In that later ruling, Lamberth reportedly called Lake’s actions arbitrary and capricious and cited Congress’s $643 million appropriation for the agency. The Reuters link is dated March 8, so it cannot by itself support the later return-to-work order; the link also returned HTTP 401 during review. The record should separate the two judicial developments or add a source for the March 17 order before treating the full sequence as verified.
subcategory: Judicial rulings on USAGM leadership and VOA layoffs

preserved_fields.title: Kari Lake Voice of America Shutdown Voided as Illegal Under Federal Vacancies Act
preserved_fields.description_short: Kari Lake Voice of America Shutdown Voided as Illegal Under Federal Vacancies Act

notes: The linked Reuters page returned HTTP 401 and is dated March 8, 2026. The supplied synopsis also describes a March 17 return-to-work order that the linked article cannot cover. The exact scope of actions voided and the later order need separate confirmation. Proposed correction: split the March 8 appointment ruling from the March 17 employee-return order, adding the latter’s source.

title: Trump Sets Thanksgiving Deadline Demanding Ukraine Sign Capitulation Peace Plan
description_short: Trump Sets Thanksgiving Deadline Demanding Ukraine Sign Capitulation Peace Plan
description_medium: In November 2025, Trump gave Kyiv about a week to accept his 28-point peace plan, with Thanksgiving Thursday described as an appropriate deadline. The proposal included territorial concessions and other terms Ukraine considered difficult. President Volodymyr Zelensky said his country faced a choice between preserving its dignity and risking the loss of U.S. support. The plan was a proposal, not an agreement signed by Ukraine.
description_long: In November 2025, Donald Trump pressed Ukraine to accept a 28-point peace plan within roughly a week and described Thanksgiving Thursday as an appropriate deadline. Reuters reported that the plan required territorial concessions and other difficult terms, while President Volodymyr Zelensky warned that Ukraine faced a choice between its national dignity and losing the United States as a partner. European allies criticized the proposal as excessively favorable to Russia. These accounts describe a proposed settlement and political pressure on Kyiv, not an agreement that Ukraine had accepted or a peace deal already in force. The short deadline put the question of continued U.S. support alongside the terms of a possible end to the war. The available source note identifies the deadline and Zelensky’s warning but does not establish that Ukraine signed, that Trump’s plan was adopted, or that the reported terms ended hostilities. The event is Trump’s demand for a rapid Ukrainian decision and the response from Kyiv and European partners. “Capitulation” is a characterization of the proposal, not the name of a signed outcome.

preserved_fields.title: Trump Sets Thanksgiving Deadline Demanding Ukraine Sign Capitulation Peace Plan
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump Sets Thanksgiving Deadline Demanding Ukraine Sign Capitulation Peace Plan
preserved_fields.description_medium: In November 2025, Trump demanded Ukraine accept his 28-point peace plan within days, setting Thanksgiving as an acceptable deadline for Zelensky to sign. Zelensky said Ukraine faced an impossible choice between national dignity and losing the US as a partner. The plan would require territorial concessions and other painful terms European allies called a capitulation to Russia.

notes: The supplied high-confidence Reuters source note says Trump gave Kyiv roughly one week, with Thursday as an appropriate deadline, and quotes Zelensky’s warning about dignity and U.S. backing. Reuters returned HTTP 401 during this turn. The description treats the plan as a proposal, not an accepted agreement.

title: The Trump administration pulls funding for Szabad Europa the Hungarian language service
description_short: The Trump administration pulls funding for Szabad Europa the Hungarian language service of Radio Free Europe after it printed opposition to Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban
description_medium: Radio Free Europe’s Hungarian service, Szabad Európa, ended operations after the Trump administration said it would no longer fund the outlet. Kari Lake told Congress its work was not aligned with U.S. national interests and said it undermined Trump’s foreign policy. The linked reporting documents the funding decision and closure, but does not establish that the service was defunded because it criticized Viktor Orbán.
description_long: Szabad Európa, the Hungarian-language service of Radio Free Europe, stopped operating in November 2025 after the Trump administration ended its funding. The service said it had worked to provide journalism and objective information to Hungarian readers and that its articles would remain available online. It had relaunched in 2020 with approval from the U.S. Agency for Global Media and Congress, following concerns about declining media freedom in Hungary under Prime Minister Viktor Orbán. Kari Lake, a senior adviser to the agency, told Congress that the service’s operations were not aligned with U.S. national interests and undermined Trump’s foreign policy. She later posted that taxpayer money should not be used to destabilize Orbán’s government through the service. The linked reporting places the closure amid broader reductions to U.S.-funded international and public broadcasters and describes Orbán’s government-aligned media environment. It establishes the funding cut and shutdown, but the available article does not show that the service was defunded specifically because it published criticism of Orbán. That causal claim in the title and synopsis needs separate evidence.
subcategory: U.S. funding cut and closure of Hungarian-language RFE service
topic_tags: U.S. Agency for Global Media funding

preserved_fields.title: The Trump administration pulls funding for Szabad Europa the Hungarian language service
preserved_fields.description_short: The Trump administration pulls funding for Szabad Europa the Hungarian language service of Radio Free Europe after it printed opposition to Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban

notes: I read the linked Yahoo/AP report; the AP page returned HTTP 403, while Yahoo carried the report. It documents the funding withdrawal, closure, Lake’s stated rationale and the service’s continued online archive. It does not establish that funding was pulled because of criticism of Orbán. Proposed correction: remove the causal “after it printed opposition” framing unless a source demonstrates that link.
